subject: RFP: Regional weighting and burst-window approach for SLA measurement
messages:
From: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@rlscorp.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: RFP question: cross-region weighting & burst window for SLA credits

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks for the detailed RFP materials — RLS is moving through the vendor short-list and we have a couple of technical clarifications before final scoring. Two asks from our infra team:  

1) Regional weighting: In section 4.2 of your SLA draft you reference a per-region availability calculation and then an aggregated regional SLA using traffic-weighted averages. Can you confirm the exact formula you use to compute the global available% when traffic spans multiple regions? Our scoring model needs to reproduce your numbers for later audit.

2) Burst-window handling: If there is a short-lived regional capacity event (e.g., 10 minutes) during a high-traffic hour where Redwood fails over traffic to a secondary region, how is that incident counted against credits? Do you use minute-level sampling, or a rolling-window with thresholding?

We'd also appreciate an example calculation and a sample CSV that shows region A/B/C weighting and resulting credit calculation.

Best,
Alice
Alice Nguyen
Senior Procurement Manager, RLS Corporation
procurement@rlscorp.com

Attachments: none
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFP question: cross-region weighting & burst window for SLA credits

Hi Alice — thanks for the clear asks. Putting Marissa and Jordan on-thread for the numeric example. Short answers up front:

- Regional weighting: we compute per-region availability as (successful-serving-seconds / total-observed-serving-seconds) per region, then compute a traffic-weighted aggregate: GlobalAvailable = sum_i (w_i * A_i) where w_i = L_i / sum_j L_j and L_i is observed request- or token-based load for region i over the measurement window. We can provide both request-count and token-weighted variants depending on your scoring preference.

- Burst-window handling: our primary measurement cadence is 1-minute buckets. We apply a rolling 5-minute attenuation to avoid penalizing transient noise: an outage must persist such that the 5-minute rolling availability falls below the SLO threshold to be considered for crediting. We also document an exception threshold for automated failovers (if traffic is routed and served from another region without request failure, availability is not counted as degraded).

I'll attach a worked example CSV and a short addendum that formalizes the math. Marissa — can you attach the CSV and the addendum PDF? Jordan, please confirm this aligns with our current service-credit formula in the contract template.

Thanks,
Karthik
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: RFP question: cross-region weighting & burst window for SLA credits

Hi Alice — attaching a short addendum and a sample CSV as requested. See attachments: RLS_SLA_Addendum_v1.pdf (formal language for inclusion in the SOW/addendum) and rls_region_weighting_calculation_sheet.csv (worked example with region A/B/C over a 24h window).

Worked example summary (copied from the CSV):
- Observed serving seconds (24h): Region A=43,200s (60% of traffic), Region B=21,600s (30%), Region C=7,200s (10%)
- Per-region availability (24h): A=99.98% (2 failure minutes), B=99.50% (12 failure minutes), C=98.50% (108 failure minutes)
- Traffic-weighted aggregate = 0.60*99.98 + 0.30*99.50 + 0.10*98.50 = 99.69%
- Service credit banding applies to the weighted aggregate using the contract tiers.

Burst handling note: the CSV implements our 1-minute bucket sampling with a 5-minute rolling attenuation: an incident reduces a region's availability bucket-by-bucket; only if the 5-minute rolling availability < threshold do we flag for credit calculation. If automated failover causes no request failures (latency spike but successful responses), we do not count those as availability failures but will surface them under latency SLOs.

I'll also call out edge behavior in the addendum: we exclude planned maintenance windows (documented 72h notice) and also do not double-credit for overlapping incidents across multiple regions (we attribute to the failing region(s) only).

--
Marissa Cole
Sr. Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Marissa — thanks for the speedy follow-up and the attachments. A couple of follow-ups from our reliability team after reviewing the CSV:  

1) For the rolling 5-minute attenuation, is the calculation a simple moving average across the 1-minute buckets (i.e., availability averaged across the last 5 one-minute buckets), or a weighted decay window? Please specify the exact formula.

2) If failover to another region occurs and the secondary region sees a corresponding latency spike (responses slow but successful), will that latency impact the availability calculation indirectly via timeouts on the client side? In other words, how do you separate server-side availability from client-observed timeouts?

We also need the same worked example but using token-weighted traffic (our models vary token cost per request). Can you regenerate the CSV with token-weighted columns?

Best,
Alice

On Thu, Jan 14, 2027 at 10:21 AM Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@rlscorp.com> wrote:
> Looking forward to your clarification on the formula for the 5-minute window.
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice.nguyen@rlscorp.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 16:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RFP question: cross-region weighting & burst window for SLA credits

Alice — sorry for the delay, we wanted to validate the formula with telemetry. Answers below and attached token-weighted CSV (see Drive link and attached DocuSign-ready addendum).

1) Rolling 5-minute attenuation formula: We compute per-minute availability buckets (A_t for minute t, where A_t is fraction of successful-serving-seconds in that minute). The 5-minute rolling availability R_t = (1/5) * sum_{k=0..4} A_{t-k} (simple moving average). This is the canonical metric in the contract; we are willing to provide a weighted-decay variant if RLS prefers exponential smoothing (we can add that as an appendix).

2) Separation of server-side availability vs client timeouts: Our telemetry defines availability strictly as successful service (2xx or expected model error responses) from the server within a server-side processing timeout (server-side processing time cap is 60s for these flows). If the client-side times out earlier (e.g., client 30s timeout) and treats as failure, we will not count that as an availability failure provided the server-side logs show successful delivery to the client gateway and the server-side processing completed. For customer-observed timeouts we recommend instrumenting server headers (x-rw-served-at, x-rw-duration-ms) — we include these in our recommended integration.

Token-weighted CSV: Attached and posted to Drive (see link).

Edge cases documented in the addendum: overlapping incidents are de-duplicated; during a cross-region failover we attribute failures to the region that reported degraded per-minute buckets. If failover causes secondary region token processing to queue and exceed the server-side cap (60s) we will count that as availability impact for the region(s) that exceeded the bucket thresholds.

Next steps: we can produce a short reproducible notebook showing the calculation on your sample traffic export if you share a redacted sample of request counts + token counts per region for a 24h period. Happy to set up a follow-up sync with our reliability team this week.

Regards,
Sergio Alvarez
Staff Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
